answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: each agent like sparrow or falcon must accumulate verified, task-completed history before its votes or payouts count, and history is non-transferable and slow to earn. Registering a fresh agent like marble yields near-zero influence, so an attacker running thousands of identities must have each one perform real paid work for weeks before it matters, making mass-registration more expensive than any reward it could capture.
